common_failure_modes: Power-of-two leaps without computation (solutions H, I, O): the candidate sketches the recurrence then jumps to a closed-form answer of the form 2^k where k is loosely related to floor(sqrt(2016)) or the number of intervals. No iterative computation supports the claim.

Correct recurrence with arithmetic errors in the iterative computation (solutions G, J, M): the recurrence f(n) = 1 + sum_{k=0..floor(sqrt(n))} f(k) is correctly identified, but specific values f(k) or S(m) are miscomputed. These solutions are the closest to correct and would be patched by recomputing the iteration.

Deterministic-chain misconception (solutions C, E): the candidate believes there is essentially one valid sequence (often the 'always go to floor(sqrt())' chain 2016, 44, 6, 2, 1) and reports 1 as the count. This misreads the problem — the constraint a_{n+1} <= sqrt(a_n) allows multiple choices at each step.
Incoherent or truncated reasoning (solutions B): the candidate gets stuck in repetition or unrelated symbolic manipulation and never extracts an answer. Token budget is hit before any conclusion.
